answer: Proof-of-personhood anchoring resists sybils: each identity must bind to a scarce external credential — a hardware attestation or a one-per-human token — so minting a new seat is not free. Like a lantern that needs real oil to burn, every account draws on a limited supply; a swarm of a thousand fakes would need a thousand genuine anchors, which no single actor can thread together. The plume of cheap clones collapses when entry demands a costly, non-replicable root.
